# Launch app
{: .no_toc }

Mint an app token (or authorization code) and open the app.
{: .fs-6 .fw-300 }

| | |
|---|---|
| **Screen ID** | `APP-03` |
| **Route** | `/apps/:appId/launch` · deep link `substratal://apps/:appId/launch` |
| **Who can use it** | Active entitlement |
| **Kind** | handoff |
| **Available in** | All Hub apps (MVP) |
| **On Linux** | `GtkUriLauncher` (OpenURI portal) |

## What's on this screen

| Element | What it is | Shows / does | Rules | On Linux |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Progress | inline spinner on tile |  | ≤ 1 s target | GtkSpinner on tile |
| Organization picker | menu | body.organization_id | only when the user has access via >1 org and the app needs org context | GtkMenuButton |

## What happens when you act

| Action | API call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Embedded launch | `POST /auth/app-tokens {application_id, organization_id?}` | 200 AppToken (5-min JWT) → open launch_url with token per app contract; never cache the token. 403 → refresh status, show APP-02; `embedded_login_not_allowed` (a third-party, self-registered app) → hosted launch below, or open `launch_url` without a token while `hosted_launch` is off. 409 → choose org. |
| Hosted launch (Phase 3) | `POST /auth/oauth/authorization-codes (PKCE S256)` | 201 → open redirect_uri?code=…&state=… in system browser / auth session |

## Good to know

- Record launch time locally for "recently launched" ordering.
